evidence.claim: AMLO said the 2022 federal budget would provide sufficient resources for social programs and guaranteed continuity for adult pensions, disability benefits, student scholarships, producer support, and strategic development works.
evidence.title: PEF 2022 garantiza continuidad de programas sociales y obras de desarrollo
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the 2022 federal budget would provide sufficient resources for social programs and guaranteed continuity for adult pensions, disability benefits, student scholarships, producer support, and strategic development works.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential budget statement; precise on priorities but self-reported.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO as president and budget agenda setter, though execution depended on ministries and later implementation.
contrary_evidence: Budget intent does not by itself prove delivery quality, coverage, or equity.

evidence.claim: AMLO said federal wellbeing programs reached 25 million households and that adults mayores and indigenous people were among the most benefited groups.
evidence.title: Programas para el Bienestar llegan a 25 millones de hogares; presupuesto prioriza a adultos mayores e indígenas, afirma presidente
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said federal wellbeing programs reached 25 million households and that adults mayores and indigenous people were among the most benefited groups.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement with concrete coverage figures, though still a self-report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct federal policy claim by AMLO; beneficiary reach still depends on implementation by agencies and local delivery systems.
contrary_evidence: Household reach alone does not prove service quality or absence of exclusion.

evidence.claim: IMSS-BIENESTAR says it was born on 31 August 2022 to guarantee free medical care and medicines for people without social security.
evidence.title: Servicios de salud IMSS-BIENESTAR
evidence.excerpt: IMSS-BIENESTAR says it was born on 31 August 2022 to guarantee free medical care and medicines for people without social security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official implementing-agency description of the new health institution and its mandate.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year founding and early rollout context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the AMLO administration and federal health restructuring, but current website language reflects later institutional consolidation.
contrary_evidence: The page also reflects later expansion and retrospective institutional framing.

evidence.claim: The 2022 minimum wage increase was 22 percent, the largest in 34 years, and the government said it directly benefited 6 million workers while recovering 71 percent of the minimum wage's purchasing power.
evidence.title: Entra en vigor incremento al salario mínimo del 22%
evidence.publisher: Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social / Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 minimum wage increase was 22 percent, the largest in 34 years, and the government said it directly benefited 6 million workers while recovering 71 percent of the minimum wage's purchasing power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary labor-policy announcement with specific wage and beneficiary figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the AMLO administration through the federal wage-setting process, though the tripartite wage commission shares formal authority.
contrary_evidence: The statement is policy intent and summary, not an independent estimate of full distributional effects.

evidence.claim: The OECD said Mexico's poverty and regional inequalities remain high, medium-term growth has weakened, weak investment and low female participation persist, and social spending and public investment have increased while health and education systems remain strained and infrastructure gaps remain significant.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico 2022
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said Mexico's poverty and regional inequalities remain high, medium-term growth has weakened, weak investment and low female participation persist, and social spending and public investment have increased while health and education systems remain strained and infrastructure gaps remain significant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral survey with explicit 2022 assessment and detailed policy diagnostics.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the target year environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partly attributable to AMLO because the report also emphasizes pandemic, structural, and long-run constraints.
contrary_evidence: The same survey says Mexico has a solid macroeconomic framework, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

evidence.claim: UNICEF says Mexico's Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners, ran government-led learning camps that reached thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and produced measurable gains in weeks.
evidence.title: Teaching at the Right Level supports learning recovery in Mexico
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF says Mexico's Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners, ran government-led learning camps that reached thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and produced measurable gains in weeks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct program case study with explicit intervention design and short-term outcome language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the education ministry under the AMLO administration, though UNICEF and partners co-implemented the intervention.
contrary_evidence: The case study itself says Mexico's education system had long faced deep inequities and severe pre-COVID foundational-skill gaps.

evidence.claim: UNICEF says Mexican children and adolescents face a triple burden of malnutrition alongside inequitable access to primary care, vaccination, and WASH, and that it supports the government with a first-1,000-days program using supplementation, breastfeeding support, vaccination, neonatal screening, and early stimulation.
evidence.title: Salud y nutrición infantil en México
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF says Mexican children and adolescents face a triple burden of malnutrition alongside inequitable access to primary care, vaccination, and WASH, and that it supports the government with a first-1,000-days program using supplementation, breastfeeding support, vaccination, neonatal screening, and early stimulation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent UN agency page with a detailed description of needs and current technical support to the government.
evidence.period_fit: Current explanatory page describing ongoing 2022-relevant conditions and interventions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to AMLO-era public-health and nutrition policy, but it is primarily an institutional support description rather than a presidential act record.
contrary_evidence: The page describes persistent structural problems, so it is not a clean success narrative.

evidence.claim: UNICEF found that children and adolescents remained the group with the highest poverty rates; indigenous children had extreme poverty of 50.2 percent and 93.9 percent lacked social security, while the first childhood cohort had poverty of 48.1 percent and the report says social-protection programs helped reduce poverty and should be universal and complemented by quality services.
evidence.title: Pobreza infantil y adolescente en México-2022
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF found that children and adolescents remained the group with the highest poverty rates; indigenous children had extreme poverty of 50.2 percent and 93.9 percent lacked social security, while the first childhood cohort had poverty of 48.1 percent and the report says social-protection programs helped reduce poverty and should be universal and complemented by quality services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent UN analysis with explicit quantitative findings on vulnerable groups and policy implications.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to federal policy because the report links reductions to social-protection programs, but it also reflects inherited inequality and structural gaps.
contrary_evidence: The same findings show large remaining deprivation and unequal access, especially for indigenous and early-childhood groups.

evidence.claim: The 2022 disability-pension program page describes a rights-based objective to improve income for people with permanent disability and explicitly links the program to reducing discrimination, racism, and marginalization affecting children, youth, indigenous people, and Afro-Mexicans with disabilities.
evidence.title: Pensión para el Bienestar de las Personas con Discapacidad Permanente
evidence.publisher: Secretaría de Bienestar / Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 disability-pension program page describes a rights-based objective to improve income for people with permanent disability and explicitly links the program to reducing discrimination, racism, and marginalization affecting children, youth, indigenous people, and Afro-Mexicans with disabilities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary program-design page with explicit target-group framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct federal program design under AMLO, though the page itself is a program description rather than an impact study.
contrary_evidence: Program design does not prove full coverage or effective delivery.

evidence.claim: The adult-pension program continued nationwide registration in October 2022, indicating ongoing expansion of the universal older-adult transfer through 2,400 local modules across the country.
evidence.title: Pensión Adultos Mayores: si cumples 65 años en septiembre u octubre ya puedes registrarte
evidence.publisher: Programas para el Bienestar / Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: The adult-pension program continued nationwide registration in October 2022, indicating ongoing expansion of the universal older-adult transfer through 2,400 local modules across the country.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary program page with clear coverage mechanics, though it is a registration notice rather than a results evaluation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct federal delivery under AMLO, while local modules and registrations are administrative implementation rather than personal action.
contrary_evidence: Registration pages show access mechanics but not actual adequacy or poverty impact.

evidence.claim: Only 57 percent of federal social programmes had a beneficiary registry, and the OECD recommended reducing fragmentation and duplication to extend coverage further, especially for low-income households.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico 2022 - Key Policy Insights
evidence.excerpt: Only 57 percent of federal social programmes had a beneficiary registry, and the OECD recommended reducing fragmentation and duplication to extend coverage further, especially for low-income households.
evidence.source_locator: key policy insights / social protection section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific structural finding from a major multilateral survey with a concrete recommendation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to federal social-policy capacity under AMLO, but it is not a direct finding of personal intent or misconduct.
contrary_evidence: The same survey says the number of social-program recipients had recently increased.

evidence.claim: The OECD said competition was weak in key sectors and that a few companies tended to dominate markets, while also warning that weak investment, informality, financial exclusion, and corruption were limiting productivity growth.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico 2022
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said competition was weak in key sectors and that a few companies tended to dominate markets, while also warning that weak investment, informality, financial exclusion, and corruption were limiting productivity growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral survey with explicit structural diagnosis and policy recommendations.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the target year environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partly attributable to AMLO because these are long-running structural conditions and market institutions, not a single presidential choice.
contrary_evidence: The survey also notes macroeconomic stability and some increases in social spending and public investment.

evidence.claim: CONEVAL's 2022 development-social-policy evaluation covers 2018-2022, identifies rising gaps and inequalities affecting indigenous populations, and says there are program gaps and a lack of integrated vision in parts of the social-policy portfolio.
evidence.title: Informe de Evaluación de la Política de Desarrollo Social 2022
evidence.excerpt: CONEVAL's 2022 development-social-policy evaluation covers 2018-2022, identifies rising gaps and inequalities affecting indigenous populations, and says there are program gaps and a lack of integrated vision in parts of the social-policy portfolio.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Domestic evaluation body with a formal mandate and explicit 2018-2022 coverage.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but explicitly centered on the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: it evaluates the federal social-policy environment under AMLO rather than one isolated program.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes advances in rights-based and course-of-life approaches.

unresolved_gaps: Federal command attribution is still thin for several state-level protest, journalist, and policing incidents.
Independent evidence that AMLO strengthened courts, the INE, INAI, or other checks is still weak compared with the evidence of media hostility and electoral-pressure attempts.
Direct personal-nexus evidence on self-enrichment, hidden ownership, or preferential benefit remains thin, and several items are still allegations or self-reports.
Independent audit-level evidence on on-time, on-budget delivery and the causal split between AMLO policy and external tailwinds is still incomplete.
